You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing the source and edited images, what does the visual evidence establish about moving the source mug to the right of the headphones: complete fulfillment, partial progress, no progress, or unresolved?
node.criteria: Compare the source mug with all visible mugs in the edited image, assess their positions relative to the same headphones, and inspect the source mug’s former location. Pass only if evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself is now to the right of the headphones. Fail only if evidence reliably establishes that the requested move made no progress. Use unknown if source-mug identity, movement, or relevant positions cannot be determined reliably. A mug on the right alone does not establish that the source mug was moved. If evidence establishes some relevant progress but not that the source mug itself reached the right side, treat that as partial progress rather than complete fulfillment or no progress.
node.binding: Cross-image binding: the source blue mug and the same headphones in the source and edited images; compare the source mug with all visible edited mugs, assess their left-to-right positions relative to the headphones, and inspect the source mug’s former location, allowing for changes in scale, lighting, and appearance.

node_traces.evidence: The source blue mug is clearly left of the headphones. In the edited image, there are two small mugs: one left of the headphones and one right, while a blue blurred shape remains near the source mug’s former location. The edited mugs’ appearance differs substantially from the source mug, so the images do not reliably establish which edited mug, if either, is the source mug. A mug is visible to the right, but its identity and movement cannot be confirmed.

response.content: {"text":"The binding currently emphasizes identity uncertainty so strongly that the node collapses to unresolved, despite visible evidence of partial progress: the source blue mug was left of the headphones, and the edited image shows a blue blurred remnant near its former location plus a mug on the right. Refine the decision logic to distinguish partial progress from complete fulfillment and no progress: assess whether the former-location remnant and right-side mug jointly support an attempted move, without treating the right-side mug alone as proof that it is the same mug. Preserve unresolved when the visual evidence genuinely cannot establish any relevant progress; do not force identity or a label. The trace is valid and has no transport, schema, or dependency failure, so focus on the semantic threshold for partial progress rather than execution. The high-confidence unresolved result is a reason to inspect that threshold, not evidence that the requested edit is absent."}
